display.title: Chuppah at Midnight
display.summary_short: For Rebbetzin Chana's birthday, memories of the Rebbe's mother, and the story of a secret midnight wedding in the home of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak in Soviet Russia.
display.summary_long: For the week of Chof-Ches Teves, Rebbetzin Chana's birthday, the storyteller tells about the Rebbe's mother and her husband, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, the rav of Yekaterinoslav. The Soviets watched him, arrested him and sent him into exile, where Rebbetzin Chana joined him and made ink from leaves and grasses so he could write down his Torah insights, later printed and often explained by the Rebbe. The storyteller then shares his own childhood memories of Rebbetzin Chana in Crown Heights: the Rebbe's daily visits to his mother, the Rebbe walking her to the door of 770 and watching until she turned the corner, and how he and his brothers held open her heavy building door. Then the story: late one night an old woman asks Reb Leivik to marry her daughter and the groom, both high officials who must keep their Jewishness secret. He quietly gathers trusted men, and when only nine come he calls the building superintendent, though he suspects him of spying. The chuppah is held in the dark with the shades drawn. Afterward two of the men throw their Communist Party cards on the table, preferring to stay with Reb Leivik.
display.lesson: Respect your parents as the Rebbe honored his mother, and being near a tzaddik makes people want to become better Jews.

date.note: 'This week, on Chof-Ches Teves, she turned 145': Rebbetzin Chana was born 28 Teves 5640, so 5785.
